title: Compat-adapter rampdown and client-assisted rewrite checklist
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and phased rollout plan to retire the temporary compatibility adapter (compat-adapter) that translates legacy chunked-SSE and batched-embeddings requests into the Unified Inference API. The goal is to provide a clear client-assisted rewrite pathway, telemetry gates, an opt-in compatibility grace window, and an automated inspection CLI to help high-volume integrators complete migration with minimal user disruption.
context: Engineering shipped a compat-adapter last year to prevent immediate breaking changes while the Unified API rolled out. Usage of the adapter has been concentrated in a small set of customers (~12 tenants) and older SDKs that rely on chunked SSE transports and batch-embed endpoints. Ops telemetry shows adapter adds 35-60ms median latency and complicates troubleshooting. The platform team needs to retire the adapter to reduce maintenance overhead and enable kernel scheduling optimizations that are incompatible with translation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a migration checklist and automated CLI tool that can detect legacy usage patterns and surface code-level fix suggestions (example snippets for Node/Python/Go).
Publish a step-by-step client migration guide with example payloads, retry semantics, and idempotency notes; guide signed off by Developer Experience and SDK leads.

Complete an internal canary where >= 80% of traffic from opt-in customers successfully uses the native Unified API for 14 consecutive days without increase in client-visible errors (5xx and protocol-level parse failures).
Define telemetry gates: adapter error rate < 0.5% and native endpoint 99th percentile latency <= adapter 99th percentile + 50ms in canary cohort before broad ramp-down.
Provide an A/B rollout plan with automatic rollback criteria tied to per-tenant SLOs (error-rate spike > 1% or P95 latency regression > 200ms).
Document migration windows, a 90-day opt-in compatibility period, and final removal date communicated 60 days in advance to affected customers.
Deliver a migration assistance program for top 10 customers with engineering timeboxed support slots and a runbook for emergency re-enable of adapter during rollback.
migration_steps: Inventory: Query usage logs to create definitive list of tenants using compat-adapter and SDK versions tied to legacy transports.
Communications: Draft customer announcement, update status page, and post migration docs to Confluence and Developer Portal.
Tooling: Ship CLI v0.9 that scans request traces, flags legacy transports, and produces suggested code diffs for replacement calls.
Canary: Invite 3 low-risk tenants to opt-in to native Unified API with feature flag; monitor metrics for 14d.
Assisted Migration: Run 2-week migration sprints with top 10 tenants; provide pull-request level guidance and sandbox endpoints.
Grace window: Open 90-day opt-in window where adapter is available but logged as deprecated; automatically tag adaptered requests for billing telemetry.
Ramp-down: After gates pass, progressively disable adapter for cohorts (internal dev tenants -> low-risk customers -> all remaining), each cohort lasting 7 days with verification checks.
Sunset: Final adapter shutdown date: disable translation service and remove feature flags; post-mortem and update service docs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Preparation, 4 weeks): inventory, docs, CLI alpha, stakeholder signoffs.
Phase 1 (Canary, 2 weeks): opt-in canary with 3 tenants; daily review and gate evaluation.
Phase 2 (Assisted Migration, 4 weeks): top-10 customers migration sprints and SDK patch releases.
Phase 3 (Public Grace Window, 12 weeks): announce 90-day deprecation window; run CLI and self-service guides.
Phase 4 (Cohort Ramp-down, 4 weeks): staged disable by cohort with telemetry gating at each step.
Phase 5 (Shutdown & Cleanup, 2 weeks): disable service, remove infra, final billing reconciliation, and post-mortem.
telemetry_gates: Canary pass condition: no increase >0.5% absolute in 5xxs and protocol parse errors for 14 days.
Latency gate: native endpoint P95 <= adapter P95 + 150ms during canary; otherwise delay ramp.
Error gate for cohort ramp: if any cohort shows error-rate increase >1% or user-facing complaints >3 in 24h, auto-pause ramp and open incident response.
Adoption target: 65% of adapter-invoking SDKs updated to Unified API before opt-in grace window closes.
Telemetry exports: flag all adapter-traced requests with migration_tag and route for per-tenant dashboards.
notes: PM note 2026-02-18: engineering prefers a 90-day grace window rather than 120; reduced window lowers maintenance but requires more proactive comms.
Design input 2026-02-23: UX sample banners for deprecated adapter and migration CTA should be in Developer Portal header; mockups in Figma link in links.
